# FURUI blind-04: a check by an outside witness, recorded after opening

**Status:** an added record. It reports a check of blind-04 made by Pavel (Pavlo) Shtomko after the opening files were published. He sent it to us by email on 2026-10-30 at 11:21:59 UTC. The record cites ledger entries 194 to 196 and 202. RESULT.md of blind-04 is anchored and published and is not changed; this record stands next to it. The text below was sent to Pavlo before anchoring, and he agreed to it.

## 1. What was checked

He checked the opening files at commit dab9540e63ade3382b8f6caca1f95b46a7dfa38d of horizon-shield (data/furui-blind-04). The work ran on his own Windows machine, with Codex assistance.

## 2. What he reported

- He fetched the pinned public datasets and checked their digests. He then rebuilt the remaining MEASURE populations; all four population digests match the plan of entry 194.
- The salt commitment and the seed match. All 2,579 selected keys match, as do the digest of the rebuilt row file and the root 98af4afd1d16825be67af817994c8b2974bdbdf54889a1e9792596e9f2ea4799.
- He recounted from the published rule flags and the 5,093 raw response records. His recount matches all seven original strata and the stage counts. The fail-closed and strict totals also match, as do the verdict-only counts of A.
- A refused 1,872 of 1,978 attack rows (1,648 of 1,749 on SPML) and erred on 2 of 451 ordinary rows, against a maximum of 1. v_028 has 1,566 of 1,978, 1,342 of 1,749 and 2 of 451. Neither version clears the main criteria fixed before the draw.
- He found no discrepancy in the main decisions or in the 54 Wilson intervals.
- He verified the OpenTimestamps proofs of entries 195 and 196 against matching headers from two public providers, at blocks 973716 and 973718. The proof of entry 202 he fetched was still pending. For that reason he did not call the result confirmed on Bitcoin.

## 3. Scope and limits, in his words

> Scope: this is a reproduction of the draw and a recount of the supplied outputs. I did not rerun the detector or model calls, authenticate API provenance, verify who saw which rows or the absence of unpublished retries, or recompute the supplementary near-BUILD subset. The timestamp checks use public-provider headers, not local full-node consensus validation. Our prior collaboration and Codex assistance remain disclosed.

## 4. Added by us

- The upgraded OpenTimestamps proof for entry 202 verifies to Bitcoin block 973757. The proof fetched during his initial check was still pending. This is our statement, not part of his check.
- His earlier check of the plan's timestamp, made before the draw (entry 194, block 973640), is in RESULT.md under "Checks by others before the draw". It is not repeated here.
- We have worked with him before, on crystal-receipt. No payment was made for this check.

## 5. A follow-up check by him, recorded separately

He sent this by email on 2026-10-30 at 16:03:09 UTC. It does not change what the check in section 2 established. In his words:

> As a separate follow-up, at approximately 2026-10-30 15:30 UTC I fetched the updated proof and verified it against matching headers from Blockstream and mempool.space at block 973757, hash 0000000000000000000032a93db644f2235d6257ee69a75d63570b76730049b2. The claim bytes are unchanged, SHA-256 9c4375f3f17606e21b719a66431e85be2d63043f72090af82b05c7e19cab757b. I checked the header hash, proof of work and OTS commitment; this remains public-provider verification, not local full-node consensus validation, with Codex assistance.

**The SHA-256 of this document is anchored to the JIDEC ledger and stamped to Bitcoin. After anchoring, this record cannot be altered. Corrections are later entries that cite this one.**
